messages:
Carlos M: quick sync - we keep getting noisy churn when rollout metadata swaps marketing labels. I'd like to propose a simple 'safety' field to decide eviction vs slow-rollout. Thoughts?

Ivy Z: love the idea. safety_level: low/medium/high? High = require explicit unpin or compat_break. Low = allow fast promotion. Medium = soft-rollout with canary.

Jun W: +1. Also add rollback_grace_seconds so authors can say how long to wait before auto-roll-back if regressions detected. Default could be 3600.

Carlos M: sketch of metadata (strings on wire): 
```
{"safety_level":"medium","rollback_grace_seconds":"3600","client_probe_endpoint":"/health/check-quick","observability_tags":"perf,quant","eviction_priority":"warm"}
```

Ivy Z: client_probe_endpoint is neat — runtime can trigger a quick diff probe against the new variant (synthetic request) to validate basic correctness before promoting. We should make probes optional and rate-limited.

Jun W: runtime logic (pseudo):
```
on_rollout_update(pin, meta):
  if meta.compat_break == "true":
    evict_immediately_and_alert()
  elif meta.safety_level == "high":
    keep_pin_until_manual_unpin()
  elif meta.safety_level == "medium":
    if meta.client_probe_endpoint:
      run_probe_then_decide(rollback_grace=meta.rollback_grace_seconds)
    else:
      start_canary(percent=0.5, deadline=now+meta.rollback_grace_seconds)
  else: # low
    promote_fast()
```

Carlos M: how to represent evict vs demote? I propose eviction_priority: hot/warm/cold and an eviction_ttl (string seconds) for warm->cold transition. Helps GC.

Ivy Z: Also add a small 'explain' field for human-readable release notes that Console surfaces: e.g., "explain":"reduce fp32->int8, expect minor perf change". Tiny details help oncall.

SRE-bot: FYI: added fields safety_level, rollback_grace_seconds, client_probe_endpoint, eviction_priority, eviction_ttl, explain to rollout proto in staging (additive).

Jun W: ops edge: global pressure must still force eviction; GC will map eviction_priority->eligible if reclaim flag set. But emit events with reason so we don't lose release intent. e.g., event: soft_promote_aborted_due_to_reclaim.

Ivy Z: also suggest a tiny 'trust_score' (0-100) set by build pipeline heuristics (coverage of tests, canary history). Runtime can combine trust_score with safety_level to decide canary size. Eg: trust_score>80 => canary 5% else 0.5%.

Carlos M: good. Example final metadata (strings): 
```
{
  "safety_level":"medium",
  "rollback_grace_seconds":"1800",
  "client_probe_endpoint":"/health/fast-check",
  "trust_score":"72",
  "eviction_priority":"warm",
  "eviction_ttl":"86400",
  "explain":"quant int8, tokenizer unchanged, small logits drift"
}
```

Jun W: action items: Carlos -> draft RFC section for safety_level semantics + default windows; Ivy -> probe spec and rate limits; Ops -> add reclaim telemetry events; SRE-bot -> wire proto change in staging and emit deploy note.

Ivy Z: open question: should safety_level be tenant-overridable? My vote: yes — tenant profile can clamp max allowed (enterprise might force high).

Carlos M: agreed. We'll add tenant_override boolean later and a lookup precedence doc in RFC.

SRE-bot: deploy-note: proto fields added safely; no breaking changes.

Carlos M: thanks team. TL;DR: add safety_level + rollback_grace + probes + trust_score + eviction hints. Will draft RFC with examples and runtime pseudocode. :white_check_mark:
